text: The last lesson walked through creating a customer end to end. Now let's slow down on three pieces of that record: the account, its sites, and its contacts, because each one holds attributes that matter constantly once a customer is live.

At the account level: payment terms, which transactions can still override. Profile class, which drives credit limit and dunning behavior. The primary salesperson, used for commissions and AutoAccounting. At the site level: tax registration, which can differ by location. Billing language and currency. And the site uses themselves, bill-to, ship-to, or both on the same address.

When a customer has multiple bill-to sites, one gets flagged primary, and that's the default unless a transaction picks another. Same idea for ship-to. Getting the primary wrong is a classic support ticket, invoices quietly default to the wrong office until someone catches it on a statement. Contacts, meanwhile, are just named people to call, attached at the party level or the account level, not application logins.

Picture Cascade Outdoor Supply opening a second warehouse in Boise. Northwind Fixtures Co adds a new account site for Boise, flagged ship-to only, while the original Spokane site stays the primary bill-to. Cascade asks that invoice questions go to Dana Reyes specifically, so Northwind adds her as a billing contact at the account level, and statement emails reference her by name from then on. Up next, lesson nine: customer profiles and credit limits.
